children: By Tatsuya Moritani / Yomiuri Shimbun Staff Writer

Chemipro Kasei Kaisha Ltd. announced Wednesday that Sudian Investment Co., an investment fund based in the British Virgin Islands that operates under a Chinese company, had acquired a 20.87% stake on a voting rights basis and become the Japanese company's largest shareholder.

The Kobe-based company listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Standard Market sold all shares held by an asset management company owned by a member of the founder's family, which had previously been the largest shareholder, to Sudian.

Chemipro Kasei holds a world-leading market share in UV absorbers, which prevent the degradation of materials used in automobiles and home appliances. It is also developing materials to enhance the power generation efficiency of perovskite solar cells.
In a large shareholding report submitted to the Kanto Regional Finance Bureau on Tuesday, Sudian stated that the purpose of its holding is "purely investment."
